data.name: Muantirah
data.gender_notes: Muantirah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic word ‘Mantar’, meaning ‘to support’ or ‘to be a supporter’. Muantirah is a name given to a girl who is brave, strong, and supportive, often used to describe a woman who stands by her loved ones through thick and thin. The name Muantirah carries the meaning “Brave, Valiant” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muantirah usually hope their child will grow to embody brave, valiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Muantirah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Brave, Valiant.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muantirah total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Muantirah reflects the cultural value placed on strong and independent women in various Islamic communities. It signifies the importance of unwavering support and encouragement in family relationships, particularly between mothers and daughters, wives and husbands, and sisters.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Muantirah also holds significant spiritual meaning. In Islam, supporting one another is a fundamental principle of faith. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, “The believers in their mutual kindness, love, and compassion are just like one body; if any limb feels pain, the whole body responds with wakefulness and fever.” (Bukhari and Muslim). The name Muantirah, thus, embodies the spiritual values of love, compassion, and support towards one’s loved ones. It serves as a constant reminder for individuals to not only be strong and independent, but also to offer support and strength to those around them.
